title: Repairs, prices and his preference for a soft tone
summary: He names the repair shops, quotes prices ($60-65, $140 for gold plate) and says he won his reputation by nice playing.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Where did you get your instruments repaired? Did the shops at Werleins and other places in
New Orleans do it? When it was Grunewald, you see, Mr. A, I'm shocked at Grunewald, another man. He used to repair it for me. Grunewald? Do you know any of those instruments repairmen there?
Well I don't know, Werleins is the one I always think about. Mr. Eckert, Mr. Eckert. Oh, Eckert, yeah. Lewis Eckert.
He's the one who used to get it fixed for me. And when I went to Grunewald, well then I never had no trouble there yet. What were the prices of those instruments
in those days? Were they quite expensive compared to them?
Sixty, sixty-five. But the busher I had to pay a hundred and forty for the busher because
it was a gold plate instrument. Did it have the best tone of the instruments

that you had or your hold? No. None of them was like the corn for tone, you know, but soft, you see, soft. But when it comes to that hard playing, like we used to have played us parades, you see, corn blasts too much and I didn't like that.
Well who would use a corn? Would those writing musicians use corn more than Holtz? Some of them. Some of them. Wouldn't make much difference. They blast on anything I guess.

It's not to say talk about it, but in truth speaking some of those instruments they blast them too much. I didn't like that. Of course it's a way of playing, you understand? But me, I won the little reputation that I did win, I won it through nice playing. That's right.
